outcomes.text: Use Italian expressions for telling time and discussing days, weeks, months and seasons.
Give dates and times, including the 24-hour clock and years, and use da, fa and fra/tra with relevant tenses.
Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles, including articles with titles and country names.
Form and recognise noun genders and singular or plural forms, including frequent irregular nouns.
Express negation using common negative words, negative pronouns and paired constructions.
Use adjectives with correct gender, number, position, comparison, superlatives and common demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative forms.
Form and position adverbs, and use adverbs for time, place, comparison, questions, quantity and common expressions.
Express common quantities.
Use subject, object, reflexive, demonstrative, interrogative, relative, disjunctive, possessive and indefinite pronouns correctly.
Place object pronouns appropriately with infinitives, gerunds and imperatives, including uses of ci, ne and ecco.
Use regular, irregular and reflexive verbs in all persons, including negative, interrogative, imperative, gerund and impersonal forms.
Use informal and formal forms of address with tu, voi and Lei.
Construct and use present, perfect, imperfect, pluperfect, future, conditional and commonly used subjunctive forms.
Use continuous, immediate-future, future-perfect, perfect-conditional and passive constructions where appropriate.
Use infinitives after verbs, with or without prepositions, including dependent infinitives and perfect infinitives.
Form conditional and subjunctive combinations, including hypothetical clauses and se clauses with present or future verbs.
Join ideas using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions for addition, contrast, choice, cause, condition and time.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers accurately.
Give information about oneself and discuss family members and friendships.
Use Italian greetings, farewells, polite expressions, introductions, thanks, apologies and ways to ask about wellbeing.
Use Italian exclamations expressing enthusiasm, annoyance, interest, disappointment, praise and thanks.
Invite someone, accept or decline invitations, and suggest alternative arrangements in Italian.
Know Italian vocabulary for family members, relationships, ages, marital status, neighbours and different stages of life.
Describe people’s physical appearance, including height, build, hair, eyes, facial hair, age, clothing accessories and voice.
Describe personality and feelings in Italian using adjectives for qualities, moods, appearance, behaviour and abilities.
Use Italian verbs for relationships and life events, including loving, embracing, marrying, being born, growing up, living and dying.
Recognise and use vocabulary for colours.
Discuss clothing, accessories and aspects of personal appearance.
Know Italian vocabulary for clothing, footwear, jewellery, bags, accessories, underwear, uniforms and seasonal garments.
Use Italian expressions for clothing sizes, fit, style, trying on, putting on, wearing, dressing and undressing.
Learn Italian vocabulary for shopping, including opening hours, banknotes, prices, shops, markets, payment methods, receipts, discounts, sizes and supermarkets.
Discuss meals, food, drinks, snacks, eating utensils and different food categories.
Know Italian vocabulary for meals, meal courses, snacks, breakfast, lunch, dinner, picnics and vegetarian or vegan food.
Know Italian vocabulary for common fruits and vegetables.
Know Italian vocabulary for meat, fish, seafood and related foods.
Know Italian vocabulary for snacks, desserts, sandwiches, pizza, crisps, soup and yoghurt.
Know Italian vocabulary for water, hot drinks, juices, soft drinks, milk and ice.
Know Italian vocabulary for staple foods, ingredients, seasonings, spreads, dairy products and vegetarian alternatives.
Know Italian vocabulary for cutlery, crockery, cookware, utensils, glasses, cups and bowls.
Use Italian adjectives describing food as cooked, raw, fresh, spicy or tasty.
Use Italian expressions and verbs for hunger, thirst, drinking, eating, dining, cooking, preparing and cutting food.
Name body parts and communicate about health, illness and related needs.
Know Italian vocabulary for major body parts, including limbs, organs, face, senses, skin and bones.
Use Italian verbs for breathing, smelling, touching and seeing.
Know Italian vocabulary for medical appointments, healthcare professionals, pharmacies, medicines and basic treatments.
Use Italian expressions for illness, symptoms, injuries, exercise, allergies, tiredness, recovery and feeling well or unwell.
Discuss travel and use vocabulary for different forms of transport.
Know Italian vocabulary for transport, journeys, tickets, luggage, stations, vehicles, passengers, tourists and travel information.
Use Italian verbs and expressions for travelling, directions, walking, driving, parking, boarding, getting off and becoming lost.
Describe rooms, household furnishings, gardens, appliances and activities at home.
Know Italian vocabulary for rooms, architectural features, furniture, doors, windows, floors, walls, stairs and ceilings.
Know Italian vocabulary for bathroom facilities, toiletries, towels, showers, mirrors, taps, soap and grooming items.
Use Italian expressions for showering, bathing, brushing teeth, washing the face and hands, and brushing hair.
Know Italian vocabulary for living-room furniture and furnishings.
Know Italian vocabulary for kitchen rooms, containers, bottles, cans, sinks and boxes.
Use Italian verbs for cooking methods, eating, sewing, freezing, preparing meals, heating, ironing and cutting food.
Know Italian vocabulary for bedrooms, beds, bedding, wardrobes, cupboards, lamps and pillows.
Use Italian expressions for getting up, sleeping, resting, napping, lying down, waking up and feeling sleepy.
Use Italian expressions for tidying the house and cleaning.
Know Italian vocabulary for gardens, plants, flowers, lawns, trees, walls, fences and garden areas.
Use Italian verbs for gardening, cultivating plants, planting flowers and growing vegetables.
Know Italian vocabulary for household appliances, electrical items, heating, cooling, cooking, cleaning and entertainment equipment.
Use Italian verbs for switching appliances on and off, opening, closing, washing, baking, repairing, pushing and taking out rubbish.
Know and use Italian words for common colours and shades.
Discuss free-time activities, hobbies and sport.
Discuss Italian leisure activities including music, singing, art, photography, gardening, television, films, reading, climbing and fishing.
Know Italian vocabulary for musical instruments and headphones, and say that an instrument is played.
Know Italian vocabulary for sports, sporting venues, equipment, competitions, teams, players, supporters, prizes and activities.
Use Italian expressions for participating in activities, taking photographs, drawing, writing, winning, losing, scoring and drawing a match.
Identify continents, countries, nationalities, people, places and compass directions.
Know the Italian names of the continents and major continental regions.
Discuss nationality, country of residence, mother tongue and foreign languages studied in Italian.
Discuss nature, the environment, climate and weather conditions.
Know and use Italian names for the four main compass directions.
Know Italian vocabulary for landscapes, natural features, resources, agriculture, climate, pollution, recycling and environmental issues.
Describe weather and climate in Italian, including temperature, precipitation, storms, wind, cloud, fog, snow, ice and forecasts.
Know Italian vocabulary for common domestic, farm, wild, flying, crawling and aquatic animals.
Discuss communication methods, digital technology, documents and written texts.
Know Italian vocabulary for digital devices, online communication, websites, social media, files, applications, security and internet content.
Learn Italian vocabulary for documents and texts, including notes, tickets, identity cards, letters, books, newspapers, magazines and online information.
Learn Italian verbs and expressions for using digital media, including uploading, clicking, connecting, copying, calling, sending, posting, publishing, saving, downloading and finding.
Describe buildings, public services, towns, cities and shopping areas.
Use vocabulary to describe size and shape.
Identify and describe common materials.
Learn Italian vocabulary for urban areas, including airports, roads, stations, markets, parks, squares, bridges, neighbourhoods, traffic and parking.
Learn Italian vocabulary for town buildings and services, including hotels, homes, libraries, cafés, cinemas, clinics, offices, hospitals, schools, stations, theatres and shops.
Learn Italian expressions for shopping and town transactions, including renting, buying, paying, returning goods, requesting refunds, complaining, spending and selling.
Learn Italian terms for units of measurement, including centimetres, kilograms, kilometres, degrees, grams, litres and metres.
Learn Italian adjectives describing size and dimensions, including high, low, short, medium-sized, enormous, large, long and small.
Learn Italian vocabulary for shapes, including circles, squares and triangles, together with their related adjectives.
Learn Italian vocabulary for materials, including silver, paper, cotton, wool, wood, metal, gold, leather, stone, plastic and glass.
Discuss schools and other educational settings, training, classrooms, equipment, subjects and studying.
Learn Italian vocabulary for education and training, including pupils, courses, school grounds, departments, headteachers, teachers, school years, subjects, students and terms.
Learn Italian vocabulary for educational institutions, including nurseries, nursery schools, primary schools, middle schools, private schools, secondary schools and universities.
Learn Italian vocabulary for classroom equipment and objects, including pencil cases, desks, bells, paper, glue, dictionaries, erasers, boards, books, pens, notebooks and rulers.

Learn Italian names for school subjects, including biology, chemistry, art, physical education, religion, physics, geography, computing, literature, languages, mathematics, music, science, history and drama.
Learn Italian vocabulary for studying, including classes, classmates, homework, questions, exams, examples, exercises, instructions, lessons, timetables, projects, breaks, results and grades.

Learn Italian verbs and expressions for studying, including understanding, asking, practising, passing or failing, experimenting, reading, taking notes, revising, answering, knowing, writing, explaining and studying.
Discuss occupations, careers and workplaces.

Learn Italian vocabulary for occupations and careers, including agricultural workers, architects, flight attendants, lawyers, waiters, drivers, dentists, doctors, tradespeople, engineers, teachers, interpreters, mechanics, police officers, soldiers and translators.
Learn Italian vocabulary for workplaces and employment, including employers, companies, employees, jobs, workshops, businesses, salaries and offices.
Learn Italian expressions for employment, including retiring, being unemployed or dismissed, being promoted, earning, working, taking holidays and finding, seeking or losing a job.
Discuss countries, nationalities and languages.

topics.title: Life in other countries and communities

outcomes.text: Discuss cultural practices, customs, religions and celebrations.

Learn Italian vocabulary for customs, religion and celebrations, including New Year, baptisms, churches, fireworks, public holidays, religious ceremonies, Christmas, Easter, pilgrimages, nativity scenes, faith and temples.
Learn Italian expressions for religious and cultural practices, including having faith, believing in something, being religious and celebrating.
